question.text: An insurance company has a liability of Rs. 10 crore due in 7 years. The CIO wants to IMMUNIZE this liability using a bond portfolio. What must the portfolio's Macaulay Duration equal?

explanation.text: The Logic: Classical single-liability immunization: Match the portfolio's Macaulay Duration to the liability's time horizon. Here, Duration = 7 years. The Trap: Matching maturity (not duration) to liability is a common error — this only works for zero-coupon bonds where duration = maturity. Manager's Pro-Tip: Immunization requires REBALANCING at every rate move — it's a semi-active discipline, not set-and-forget.
